corrections_and_extensions: Variance is E[X^2]-(E[X])^2; missing square in a spoken zero-mean formula does not change the numerical example.
Discrete-time indexing is not a claim that physical time cannot be subdivided.
A fixed-time central limit theorem alone does not prove path-space convergence or the full Brownian process law.
A finite piecewise-linear random walk is differentiable between mesh points; nowhere-differentiability is an almost-sure Brownian limit property.
At non-grid times the step-process variance uses floor(t/dt)*dt; variance t is exact at mesh times and in the limit.
The diffusion PDE is for a density under regularity, with a delta initial measure interpreted weakly; finite lattice masses are not continuous density values.
